resources.string: A simplified view of normal hemostasis at a small gap in a blood vessel. These events overlap in the body; sizes and timing are not to scale.
A small gap in the vessel wall
A small break in the vessel lining exposes collagen in the wall to the passing blood.
Platelets attach to the exposed wall
Von Willebrand factor, a blood protein, helps passing platelets catch and attach where collagen is exposed.
The attached platelets change shape and release signals that help activate nearby platelets.
More platelets stick to one another at the gap. This cluster of platelets is the platelet plug.
As blood coagulates locally, fibrin forms a mesh through and around the platelet plug, helping hold it in place.
